what_to_add: Choose one canonical host; make robots.txt and sitemap.xml return direct 200 responses; render visible HTML with unique title/H1/body/internal links; eliminate www↔apex redirect loops; ensure /hi/ is rendered or remove the alternate until ready.
observed_evidence: gocoupon.io homepage returned 200 but only 6 extractable words, 0 H1s, 0 links, and 0 images; robots.txt and sitemap.xml alternated between 308 and 307 redirects.
why_it_matters: A large content library cannot compete reliably if search engines receive an almost-empty shell or cannot fetch crawl files.
first_sprint_scope: Fix host redirects; publish SSR/SSG homepage; add direct robots.txt and sitemap.xml; validate with URL Inspection and a rendered crawl.

what_to_add: Create 10–20 high-priority merchant pages with live verified offers, coupon code/deal separation, restrictions, last-tested timestamp, success/failure reporting, FAQs, store overview, and internal links to category and editorial pages.
observed_evidence: GrabOn sitemap inventory contained 3,750 merchant URLs; CouponDunia contained 3,383 store URLs. GrabOn and CouponDunia representative pages expose many offers, filters, freshness, activity, and explanatory sections.
why_it_matters: Merchant-intent pages are the closest organic path to coupon conversions; the target currently exposed no crawlable store URL in the public sitemap/crawl.
first_sprint_scope: Launch 10 canonical merchant pages; create a reusable template; only expand when every page has real, unique offer data.

what_to_add: Add category hubs with merchant lists, buying intent guidance, current deal modules, FAQs, breadcrumbs, and links to every active merchant page; keep each hub indexable and maintained.
observed_evidence: GrabOn sitemap contained 172 category URLs; CouponDunia contained 121 category URLs; goCoupon exposed only its homepage.
why_it_matters: Category hubs create topical structure and distribute internal authority between the homepage, merchants, and articles.
first_sprint_scope: Publish 8 hubs; link from navigation and homepage; add ItemList/BreadcrumbList only when the listed items are visible.

what_to_add: Show exact code, offer type, eligibility, expiry or no-expiry state, last-tested time in IST, test outcome, restrictions, merchant source, user feedback, and change history; do not invent success rates or ratings.
observed_evidence: GrabOn shows verified status, last-checked timestamp, success percentages, usage counts, filters, and FAQs. CouponDunia shows deal/coupon/cashback separation, People Used Today, ratings, and current-date page headings.
why_it_matters: Coupon pages compete on confidence and freshness as much as on title tags; transparent evidence can differentiate a newer domain from older aggregators.
first_sprint_scope: Add the data fields and UI to the merchant template; log every verification event; expose only factual structured data.

what_to_add: Explain auto-apply behavior, supported stores, permissions, privacy, coupon testing, cashback stacking, browser troubleshooting, and extension installation with screenshots or a short demo; link to merchants.
observed_evidence: goCoupon’s current metadata positions it as an auto-apply Chrome extension and already declares SoftwareApplication and FAQPage structured data, while competitor pages emphasize how-to instructions and FAQs.
why_it_matters: This is the target’s differentiated product advantage; it is more defensible than copying generic coupon-list content.
first_sprint_scope: Publish 6 utility pages; make the main answer visible in HTML; add HowTo/BreadcrumbList/SoftwareApplication only where content supports it.

what_to_add: Build three clusters: store-specific sale calendars and buying guides; coupon/cashback explainers; and seasonal/bank-offer guides. Every article should link to live merchant pages and state update dates and sources.
observed_evidence: GrabOn’s blog sitemap reports 438 posts with active 2026 seasonal content and many categories. CouponDunia’s blog sitemap reports 665 posts, but the visible archive has a large 2014–2015 legacy tail plus a smaller current update set.
why_it_matters: The target needs useful, commercially connected editorial content rather than a high-volume generic lifestyle archive.
first_sprint_scope: Publish 12 strong articles: 4 explainers, 4 store/sale guides, 4 seasonal or bank-offer pages; refresh monthly.

what_to_add: Create transparent comparisons with methodology, update dates, supported stores, verification approach, privacy model, coupon coverage, cashback behavior, and clear pros/cons; do not make unverifiable superiority claims.
observed_evidence: CouponDunia’s current blog includes a “Best Cashback Websites in India 2026” comparison-style article; the live search sample also shows comparison and coupon-site queries occupied by established publishers and aggregators.
why_it_matters: Comparison intent can attract users already evaluating coupon tools, but it should follow the core merchant and utility pages.
first_sprint_scope: Publish 2 factual comparison pages after collecting verifiable product data; add tables and author/editor review metadata.

recommended_target: /hi/ and selected Hindi merchant or guide pages
what_to_add: Make the Hindi alternate a real, translated, internally linked experience with matching canonicals/hreflang; do not publish an empty alternate page.
observed_evidence: goCoupon homepage HTML declares hreflang en-in, hi, and x-default, but the crawl found only one public homepage URL and no rendered Hindi content.
why_it_matters: A language alternate without indexable translated content can dilute signals and creates a poor user experience.
first_sprint_scope: Either render /hi/ with complete localized content and reciprocal hreflang or temporarily remove it from the head.

what_to_add: Keep WebSite, Organization, SoftwareApplication, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage, Offer, and ItemList markup aligned with visible content; add XML sitemap entries for every canonical indexable route; ensure no orphan pages.
observed_evidence: goCoupon’s homepage contains multiple JSON-LD blocks, but the visible body is empty; GrabOn and CouponDunia expose large crawlable inventories and deep templates.
why_it_matters: Schema cannot substitute for visible, crawlable content; aligned markup can reinforce a technically sound information architecture.
first_sprint_scope: Build automated checks for status, canonical, indexability, H1, visible text, JSON-LD-to-visible-content consistency, and sitemap inclusion.
